subject.title: fix(config): warn when JSON5 comments are lost on config write

question: Should ConfigWriteResult and ConfigReplaceResult permanently expose an optional warning field through the plugin SDK, or should comment-loss diagnostics remain internal to human-facing config workflows?
rationale: The patch is mechanically sound, but the repository treats plugin API and config result surfaces as compatibility-sensitive; automation cannot choose the permanent public contract.

options.title: Approve the structured diagnostic
options.body: Accept the optional warning fields as additive plugin API, add focused contract coverage where needed, and require public-path terminal proof before merge.

options.title: Keep the API unchanged
options.body: Remove the result fields and limit the warning to human-facing write paths, accepting that skipOutputLogs callers will not receive the diagnostic.

options.title: Pause for preservation design
options.body: Defer this mitigation if maintainers want comment-preserving mutation rather than a warning-based contract.

recommendation.title: Approve the structured diagnostic
recommendation.body: Accept the optional warning fields as additive plugin API, add focused contract coverage where needed, and require public-path terminal proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the broadest involvement in config write, schema, and plugin configuration contract changes.
